subject: Clarify marketplace crediting and per-token commit implications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Acme Analytics <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T09:15:00Z
Subject: Clarify marketplace crediting and per-token commit implications

Hi Alex and team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We covered the usage profile and the two commit paths you were evaluating (hosted direct commit vs. buying via AWS Marketplace). A few quick notes to surface differences that matter for how discounts and credits will behave on your side: 

- Marketplace billing (AWS) is invoiced through AWS and normally appears as a marketplace line item. AWS charges a marketplace fee and then passes the remainder to Redwood. Because the invoice is from AWS, Redwood’s direct billing systems don’t receive token-by-token usage in real time for crediting against a direct commit.
- For per-token commits (hosted direct): tokens are accounted on Redwood’s platform and applied immediately to the committed bucket for discounting and overage calculations.
- Practical impact: if you want a guaranteed per-token discount to apply uniformly across all usage, the cleanest approach is to have the commit on a direct hosted contract. Marketplace purchases can be credited toward a commit, but it requires monthly reconciliation and explicit pass-through/crediting terms in the contract.

Attached: Acme_Redlines_v3.pdf (contract redlines) and pricing_matrix_marketplace_vs_direct.xlsx (side-by-side).

Ask: can you confirm whether Acme needs the invoice to come through AWS for procurement/PO flow, or if a direct Redwood invoice is acceptable for the committed portion? If AWS is required, we should: 

1) agree on a reconciliation cadence (monthly) and a specific crediting formula (we propose gross usage reported by AWS multiplied by (1 - marketplace fee) credited to your Redwood commit), and
2) add a short clause to the SOW/MSA that defines how marketplace-billed spend will be recognized against the commit.

Happy to jump on a quick call to align.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace crediting and per-token commit implications

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of clarifying questions from our procurement/legal team: 

1) When marketplace spend is "credited" toward a commit, what documentation will we receive each month? We need line-item evidence that shows raw token counts so our internal chargeback works.
2) What's the expected lag between AWS invoice posting and Redwood applying a credit? We need to know if any timing mismatch will cause month-to-month overages on our finance side.
3) Are there any restrictions on stacking marketplace discounts with promotional commit tiers? For example, if Redwood offers a 20% commit discount and AWS discounts result in an additional pass-through, can these stack or is the calculation net of marketplace fees?

Procurement note: Acme strongly prefers marketplace billing due to our central vendor policy, but we can be flexible if the crediting path is robust.

Alex Morgan
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
procurement@acme-analytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Acme Analytics <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Billing <aws-marketplace-ops@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace crediting and per-token commit implications

Alex —

Great questions. Short answers and a proposed operational workflow below.

1) Documentation: AWS provides line-item usage reports for Marketplace metered products (CSV). Redwood will accept the AWS CSV export and run an automated reconciliation that outputs a monthly "Marketplace Credit Report" showing: gross token counts, AWS marketplace fee %, net tokens credited to the Redwood commit, and resulting dollar credit. We will provide that report as a PDF and a CSV export for your finance system.

2) Timing: typical cadence is AWS posts marketplace reports within 5 days after month-end. Redwood will ingest and apply credits within 7 business days of receiving the AWS report. That means credits will typically appear on the following Redwood month statement. We can add a clause to the SOW to define this 7-business-day SLA.

3) Stacking rules: our proposal is to credit the net value after marketplace fees toward the commit (i.e., credits are calculated on gross usage less the AWS marketplace fee). Commit discounts apply to the portion of spend recognized by Redwood after crediting. Practically this means: 

- Example: 100M tokens billed via AWS, AWS fee 10% => 90M tokens net to Redwood. The 90M tokens are counted against your commit and the commit discount applies per our agreed tier.

If you need the accounting to show the 100M as counted for internal consumption despite fees, we can include a mapping table in the reconciliation but the economic credit on our books must reflect the net we receive from AWS.

Next steps (proposed):
- Sign off on the reconciliation clause we will add to the SOW (I attached a draft redline in Acme_Redlines_v3.pdf).
- Confirm acceptance of monthly cadence and 7-business-day application.
- If accepted, Redwood will prepare the Marketplace Credit Report template and share a sample CSV based on a synthetic month for validation.

Ive attached a pricing matrix that shows a simple numeric example for the common commit tiers side-by-side (pricing_matrix_marketplace_vs_direct.xlsx).

Regards,
Karthik

Date: 2027-06-17T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace crediting and per-token commit implications

Quick internal note / next steps for deal ops: 

- Acme confirmed preference for AWS Marketplace but is open to the reconciliation approach.
- Sean: please prepare the short SOW clause and a sample Marketplace Credit Report template (CSV + PDF). Use the example Karthik outlined (gross tokens -> subtract AWS fee -> net credited tokens). We will need this for legal/finance sign-off.
- Karthik: schedule a 30-min call with Acme procurement and our deal ops next week to walk through the sample CSV and the timing impact (monthly lag, 7-business-day application).

Attachments: I reviewed Acme_Redlines_v3.pdf and left two inline comments on billing clause. If legal wants to push back on any language that ties credit application to AWS report delivery, call it out. 

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
